Administrative Assistant Resume Example & Writing Guide (2026)

An administrative assistant resume is judged on one question: can the office run smoothly because of you? Hiring managers — and the applicant tracking systems that screen before them — scan your resume for the signals that answer it: who you supported and at what scale, how many calendars, trips, and expense reports you actually processed, the office software you know by name, and proof that you handle confidential information without drama.

This guide gives you a full annotated example, a section-by-section breakdown, the office-management keywords postings screen for, and the mistakes that quietly cost administrative assistants interviews.

Quick answer: An administrative assistant resume should include a summary naming your office environment and strongest operational proof (e.g. administrative assistant supporting 4 executives across 3 time zones), a skills section with Microsoft 365, scheduling and expense tools, experience bullets with numbers (calendars managed, travel itineraries booked, expense volume processed), and keywords mirrored from the posting. Proof of reliability wins.

Key Takeaways

  • Lead with who you support and at what scale — “administrative assistant supporting 4 executives across 3 time zones” answers the credibility question in one line.
  • Every experience bullet needs a number: meetings coordinated, itineraries booked, expense reports processed, events run, documents produced. “Provided admin support” is a claim; “processed 200+ expense reports totaling $340K with 98% first-pass approval” is evidence.
  • Spell software exactly as postings do — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Concur, Expensify, SharePoint — they are literal ATS keyword filters.
  • Name confidentiality explicitly. Assistants who handle executive inboxes, HR files, or financial data are trusted with the company’s secrets; one line of discretion proof belongs on every experienced admin resume.
  • Keep the layout single-column with standard headings. Fancy graphics don’t parse. Verify with a free ATS scan before you apply.

What Admin Hiring Managers Actually Look For

Ask the executive or office manager doing the hiring what separates a keep-forever assistant from a risky one and it won’t be “organized.” It’ll be:

  • Reliability at scale. Calendars managed, meetings coordinated, travel booked, expense reports processed — with zero dropped balls. “Coordinated 120+ meetings a year across 3 time zones with zero double-bookings” is the line everything else supports.
  • Proactive problem-solving. Catching the conflicting meeting before the executive does, rerouting the canceled flight before it matters, having the board packet ready before it’s asked for. Show one story where you fixed something before it became a problem.
  • Software fluency. Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Excel, Teams, SharePoint), Google Workspace, Concur or Expensify, Zoom, scheduling tools. Assistants are the company’s power users — name the tools.
  • Discretion. Executive inboxes, HR files, board materials, financial data. “Handled confidential correspondence for the C-suite” signals the trust level you’ve earned.
  • Event and project ownership. All-hands meetings, client visits, office moves, onboarding weeks. Owning logistics end-to-end is how assistants become office managers.

If your resume reads like a list of tasks you were assigned, it will lose to one that reads like a record of the chaos you prevented.

Administrative Assistant Resume Example (Annotated)

Below is a complete example for an administrative assistant in a corporate office. It’s fictional — the names and companies are illustrative — but every bullet follows the pattern admin hiring managers respond to: the environment up front, numbers on every role, and the office vocabulary spelled exactly as postings use it.

DANIEL OKAFOR
Abuja, FCT · (234) 555-0198 · daniel.okafor@email.com

SUMMARY
Administrative assistant with 5 years supporting executives and operations teams in professional-services firms. Coordinated 120+ meetings a year across 3 time zones with zero double-bookings; processed 200+ expense reports totaling $340K with 98% first-pass approval. Trusted with C-suite correspondence and confidential HR files.

SKILLS
Calendar management · Travel coordination · Expense reporting (Concur, Expensify) · Meeting and event logistics · Inbox management · Data entry (95 wpm, 99% accuracy) · Onboarding support · Vendor management · Confidentiality · Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Excel, Teams, SharePoint) · Google Workspace · Zoom · Slack

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Administrative Assistant — Meridian Advisory Partners, Abuja | 2022–Present

  • Support 4 partners across Abuja, Lagos, and London time zones; manage 120+ meetings a year with zero double-bookings.
  • Process 200+ expense reports annually (approx. $340K) with 98% first-pass approval — cut reimbursement cycle from 9 days to 4.
  • Coordinate quarterly all-hands and client events (60–120 attendees): venues, catering, travel, agendas; came in 12% under budget 4 quarters running.
  • Handle confidential correspondence, board materials, and HR files for the leadership team; sole gatekeeper of the partners’ shared inbox.
  • Onboarded 22 new hires in 2 years: equipment, accounts, induction schedules — reduced setup time from 5 days to 2.

Office Assistant — Brightwell Logistics, Abuja | 2020–2022

  • Managed front-desk operations for a 40-person office: visitor sign-in, courier scheduling, meeting-room booking across 6 rooms.
  • Maintained office-supply and vendor relationships; renegotiated the cleaning contract for 18% annual savings.
  • Produced weekly operations reports from Excel trackers; typing 95 wpm with 99% accuracy on data-entry audits.
  • Coordinated 30+ domestic travel itineraries a year: flights, hotels, ground transport, per-diem advances.

EDUCATION
HND, Office Technology and Management — 2020

Section-by-Section Breakdown

Summary: environment, tenure, and headline proof in three lines

The example opens with “administrative assistant” — role and tenure — then the proof: 120+ meetings, zero double-bookings, $340K in expenses at 98% first-pass approval. If you’re entry-level, lead with transferable proof instead: “coordinated schedules for a 20-person volunteer team; managed cash reconciliation and supply orders with zero discrepancies.”

Skills: software and admin vocabulary exactly as postings spell them

Admin postings are keyword-dense, and applicant tracking systems screen for exact terms. Name your software (Microsoft 365, Outlook, Concur, Expensify, SharePoint), your functions (calendar management, travel coordination, expense reporting, onboarding support), and your speed/accuracy if it’s strong (95 wpm, 99% accuracy). “Good organizer” is not a keyword; “Concur” is.

Experience: every bullet pairs an action with a number

The pattern is verb + scope + metric: “managed 120+ meetings a year across 3 time zones”; “cut the reimbursement cycle from 9 days to 4.” Savings and cycle-time improvements are gold — they translate office work into business outcomes a hiring manager can price.

Discretion: show the trust level you’ve earned

Assistants who handle executive correspondence, HR files, or financial data carry the company’s secrets. One line naming what you’ve been trusted with — without disclosing anything sensitive — separates you from candidates who’ve only run front desks.

Administrative Assistant Skills & ATS Keywords

Mirror the posting’s exact language and keep these groups on your resume:

  • Operations: calendar management, inbox management, travel coordination, meeting and event logistics, vendor management, onboarding support.
  • Financial: expense reporting, Concur, Expensify, invoice processing, budget tracking, per-diem advances.
  • Software: Microsoft 365, Outlook, Excel, Teams, SharePoint, Google Workspace, Zoom, Slack.
  • Professional: confidentiality, data entry, 95 wpm, front-desk operations, meeting-room booking, board materials.

Check your resume against a free ATS scan — for example, Cvyon's ATS grader — before you apply. Administrative assistants lose interviews to parsing failures they never see: two-column layouts and icon-heavy designs are the usual killers. Start from a clean template in the template gallery or the resume builder, then verify with the free ATS grader.

5 Mistakes That Cost Administrative Assistant Interviews

  1. Listing duties instead of outcomes. “Responsible for the office” is a job description, not a resume bullet. Replace every duty with a number: meetings coordinated, trips booked, reports processed, savings negotiated.
  2. Generic software claims. “Proficient in Microsoft Office” wastes a line. Name the apps and your depth: “Outlook (shared inboxes, rules); Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP); SharePoint (permissions, libraries).”
  3. No discretion signal. If you’ve handled confidential information and never say so, a hiring manager can’t distinguish you from someone who hasn’t. One line is enough — and never disclose actual secrets.
  4. Graphics that don’t parse. Star ratings, skill bars, and calendar-icon visuals look great and parse terribly. ATS software reads text, not design — single column, standard headings.
  5. Ignoring the company’s own vocabulary. If the posting says “expense reporting in Concur” and you write “handled travel costs,” the ATS filter never fires. Mirror the posting’s exact terms.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should be included in an administrative assistant resume?

A summary naming your office environment and strongest operational proof (e.g. “administrative assistant supporting 4 executives across 3 time zones”); a skills section with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, scheduling and expense tools (Concur, Expensify), and office-management vocabulary; experience bullets with numbers — calendars managed, events coordinated, expense volume processed, onboarding supported; and keywords mirrored from the posting.

How do I quantify administrative assistant work on a resume?

Attach a number to every responsibility: executives and teams supported, meetings scheduled per week, travel itineraries booked, expense reports processed and their dollar volume, events coordinated and attendee counts, documents or reports produced, onboarding checklists completed. “Managed the CEO’s calendar” is a claim; “coordinated 120+ meetings a year across 3 time zones with zero double-bookings” is proof.

Do I need a cover letter for an administrative assistant role?

A cover letter helps for executive-assistant and office-manager-track roles, where writing quality IS the skill being tested. Keep it to three short paragraphs: the office you’re supporting, one measurable proof of reliability, and why you want this company. For high-volume admin postings, a strong summary on the resume alone is usually enough.

Should an administrative assistant resume be one page?

Yes — one page for administrative assistant roles. Hiring managers and applicant tracking systems both prefer a clean single page with standard headings. Executives you’ll support value concision; the resume is your first demonstration of it. Two pages is only defensible for office-manager candidates with 10+ years and team-lead scope.

What skills do employers want most on an administrative assistant resume?

Calendar and inbox management, travel coordination, expense reporting (Concur, Expensify), meeting and event logistics, data entry with high accuracy, office-supply and vendor management, onboarding support, and confidentiality with sensitive information. Software keywords matter: Microsoft 365, Outlook, Excel, SharePoint, Google Workspace, Zoom, Teams — spell them exactly as postings do.

How do I write an administrative assistant resume with no experience?

Reframe any organizational experience as admin proof: “coordinated schedules for a 20-person volunteer team”; “managed cash reconciliation and supply orders for a campus club.” Add a skills section (Office 365, scheduling, data entry, customer service), any office or retail volunteering, and one line about typing accuracy if it’s strong. Run it through a free ATS grader before applying.
